name: Central bank stress
summary: Bank of England decides on 5 Nov with a rise widely expected; Fed and ECB on hold
state: The Fed held at 3.75–4% on 28 Oct after a September hike, and the ECB held at 2.50% on 29 Oct, warning of upside inflation and downside growth risks. The Bank of England decides on 5 Nov with a rise widely expected, and Egypt raised rates on 29 Oct. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move had been made as of 2 Nov.
for_you: Interest rates are more likely to rise than fall in the near term in the US and UK, which affects mortgages, loans and savings rates.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma across G7 central banks = Watch

sources.title: Bank of England rate decision, 5 Nov 2026 (calendar)

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
